To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
what companies do is more important than what they say, and that what companies do in terms of socially responsible acts sustains the financial value of their CSR.
the association between CSR and firm financial performance is stronger for what companies do than what they say, and that this association is stronger for MNCs than for non‐MNC firms.
what companies do based upon KLD ratings is positively associated with overall financial performance and that the association is driven by MNCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the financial value of global CSR and the association between corporate and stakeholder interests in a less regulated business environment.
how to sustain the financial value and performance of global CSR in a less‐regulated business environment.
the business case for doing good while making a good profit.

the greater unifying of both profit maximizing and stakeholder interests in corporate acts, not corporate statements alone, will continue to sustain the financial value and global relevance of CSR.
